scope: Proposition 5.12 (Opened conditional derivatives) of the manuscript “Cutoff throughout the high-temperature Sherrington–Kirkpatrick phase” (preprints/Cutoff-throughout-the-high-temperature-Sherrington-Kirkpatrick-phase-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 227 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 d99d391c8c3ed79f), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 52. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix a smooth multitime calculation as in Theorem 4.4, a finite causal tree, common Duhamel and likelihood truncations from Theorem 4.5, and the tensor approximations of Theorem 5.10. Require every linear-query edge of the calculation and every opened K edge to belong to the admitted path-matrix algebra, with its entry predictions, and require all bounded coefficient labels to be admitted path labels. In particular, the calculation values are admitted path recipes; the likelihood calculations above use J and J◦J as their query matrices. The broader class of arbitrary bounded-operator query maps in Theorem 4.4 is not asserted to have this closure. After ordinary conditional expectations are opened on their specified causal branches, every remaining derivative contraction is a bounded path matrix up to successive operator-norm errors. It has vanishing off-diagonal maximum and the Hadamard and diagonal predictions of Theorem 5.8. The network errors have the typical, weighted and integrated-parameter meaning of Theorem 4.6. The earlier tensor and conditional truncation errors are uniform in the joining state and stored parameters.
